facts.value: Education can be described as the ‘wise, hopeful and respectful cultivation of learning undertaken in the belief that all should have the chance to share in life’. The process of education flows from a basic orientation of respect – respect for truth, others and themselves, and the world.

facts.value: For teachers to be educators they must consider people’s needs and wishes now and in the future, reflect on what might be good for all (and the world in which we live), and plan their interventions accordingly.

source.title: Attending to people’s feelings, experiences and needs + Learning particular things

metadata.chunk_title: Attending to people’s feelings, experiences and needs + Learning particular things

facts.value: How do we balance individual needs and wishes against what might be good for others? This is something that should be answered on a case-by-case basis, and it is likely to be a focus for conversation and reflection in the work with people.

source.title: Attending to people’s feelings, experiences and needs + Learning particular things

facts.value: What do we do when people do not see the point of learning things – for example, around grammar or safety requirements? We must ask and listen, weigh this against the significance of these things in life, and any curriculum or health and safety or other requirements we have a duty to meet.

facts.value: Failing to attend to people’s feelings and experiences is problematic. It reveals a basic lack of respect for them and is counter-productive when people are not ready to look at the things we are trying to explore.

facts.value: Recent developments in brain science have underlined the significance of learning from experience from the time in the womb. Bringing people’s experiences into the classroom or learning situation is fundamental to the learning process.
